business_process: Remote patient monitoring and secondary alarm notification (DDC)
description: DDC receives VM-700 and VM-500 telemetry through DG-10 gateways; clinicians view patients remotely; secondary alarm notifications and results go to hospital EHRs and clinical communication systems
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 2,300 hospitals use remote viewing and secondary alarms to staff units; primary alarms still sound at the bedside, which caps safety impact at Moderate; BAAs and SL-1 contracts carry 99.9% availability commitments; data older than 15 minutes has little value for remote monitoring
manual_workaround: Hospitals switch to bedside and central-station monitoring under their downtime procedures; monitors buffer 72 hours of trends locally and backfill when the DDC returns
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; hospital networks and EHR interface engines; notification service provider
dependent_people_or_facilities: DDC site reliability team (24x7); SOC; customer support
quantified_impact_basis: SL-1 service credits (about $0.35 million a day at the 99.9% commitment) plus incident response and customer support surge; contract loss risk is reputational and not counted
single_points_of_failure: Single primary region for the DDC ingestion tier (warm standby in a second region)

business_process: Remote cardiac monitoring: ECG event review and urgent physician notification (RCM)
description: CR-100 patches stream ECG through the phone gateway app to the RCM platform; the arrhythmia algorithm flags events; cardiac technicians review and call urgent findings to the prescribing physician
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 16,000 patients are monitored at any time; urgent arrhythmias must reach a physician quickly, so patient safety drives the 4-hour MTD; the phone app buffers about 24 hours of ECG and backfills, which supports a 15-minute RPO for events already received; practice contracts set report turnaround times
manual_workaround: Technicians in the unaffected monitoring center take over; if the platform itself is down, patients are told through the app and practices by phone to use symptom-triggered emergency instructions; ECG backfills when the platform returns
dependent_systems: SYS-02; SYS-08; SYS-11 (CR-100 and phone gateway app)
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; mobile operating system platforms and app stores; telephony carrier for urgent calls
dependent_people_or_facilities: 700 RCM staff in the Florida and Texas monitoring centers
quantified_impact_basis: About $0.9 billion a year of RCM revenue is earned per monitoring day (about $2.5 million a calendar day); customers are not charged for unmonitored days; safety impact dominates
single_points_of_failure: RCM platform recovered in 3.5 h against a 2 h RTO in the 2026-04-18 DR test (POAM-026)

business_process: Drug library and firmware update distribution (DDC update service)
description: Update service delivers signed firmware to VM-700, DG-10, and IV-300 v2 devices and approved drug libraries to IV-300 pumps; field service installs VM-500 and IV-300 first-generation updates by USB
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Pumps keep running on their current drug library, so a short outage is tolerable; an out-of-cycle security fix must reach the field as soon as possible under 524B(b)(2)(B) and within the 60-day window in FDA's postmarket guidance; images are rebuilt from the artifact repository, so 24 hours of RPO is enough
manual_workaround: Field service installs urgent fixes by USB; hospitals apply compensating network controls from the customer advisory; pharmacists load drug libraries locally where the pump model supports it
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; content delivery network
dependent_people_or_facilities: DDC site reliability team; field service
quantified_impact_basis: Field service overtime for USB installs and customer support calls
acquired_business_dependency: IV-300 first-generation module uses per-hospital pre-shared keys to reach the drug library service
single_points_of_failure: Update service depends on the artifact repository and the signing service (BP-04)

business_process: Device software build, code signing, and release (Device Software Factory)
description: Build, test, sign, and release firmware and cloud software for all product lines; generate SBOMs; publish released images to the update service and to plant programming stations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: No security fix can ship without the build pipeline and the HSM signing service (524B(b)(2)(B)); plants hold cached released images for about 2 weeks of production, so production is not stopped immediately; source code is in the SaaS repository with continuous replication, so a 1-hour RPO is achievable for build metadata
manual_workaround: Engineers keep working on local clones; emergency releases wait for the secondary HSM at DC-2; plants keep producing from cached released images
dependent_systems: SYS-04; SYS-05 (PLM release records); SYS-08; SYS-09 (DC-1, DC-2)
dependent_third_parties: Source repository SaaS vendor; HSM vendor support; Cloud provider B (cloud runners); PLM vendor
dependent_people_or_facilities: About 1,100 device software engineers; build and release engineering; DC-1 and DC-2
quantified_impact_basis: About 1,100 engineers idle or delayed (about $1,000 a day each); release and submission schedule slips are not counted
acquired_business_dependency: IV-300 1.x firmware is signed on a standalone offline signing workstation (POAM-001)
single_points_of_failure: Legacy IV-300 signing workstation has one copy of its key and no backup key share

business_process: Product security vulnerability intake, coordinated disclosure, and customer advisories (PSIRT)
description: CVD intake from researchers, the ISAO, CISA, and customers; triage; controlled or uncontrolled risk decisions; customer advisories and public disclosure
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: An exploited vulnerability is a patient safety and regulatory event; the published CVD policy commits to acknowledgment within 3 business days; FDA's postmarket guidance sets 30-day customer communication for uncontrolled risk; a lost report can lead to uncoordinated public disclosure
manual_workaround: Researchers, the ISAO, and hospitals reach the PSIRT by the phone number in the CVD policy; triage continues in the offline case template and moves to the case system on recovery
dependent_systems: SYS-05 (eQMS); SYS-09 (productivity suite and PSIRT case system); SYS-08
quantified_impact_basis: Staff time only; the impact is regulatory and reputational
single_points_of_failure: None (two intake channels: web form and monitored phone line)

business_process: Complaint handling, medical device reporting, and correction and removal reporting
description: Complaint intake and investigation; MDRs (21 CFR 803); correction and removal reports (21 CFR 806); records under 21 CFR 820.35
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Regulatory clocks run in days: 5 work days (803.53), 10 working days (806.10), 30 calendar days (803.50); losing complaint records would be a Severe regulatory impact, so the RPO is 4 hours
manual_workaround: Paper complaint form and a controlled spreadsheet log kept by Quality; FDA electronic submissions prepared from a clean workstation
dependent_systems: SYS-05 (eQMS); SYS-07 (ERP for UDI traceability); SYS-08
dependent_third_parties: eQMS SaaS vendor; FDA electronic submission gateway
dependent_people_or_facilities: Quality and regulatory staff (900); customer support
quantified_impact_basis: Staff overtime for manual logging and back-entry
acquired_business_dependency: MN-1 complaint records for IV-300 moved into the eQMS in 2025; legacy records are read-only in an archive

business_process: Patient monitor and gateway production (Plant FL-1)
description: Build, test, program, and release VM-700 monitors and DG-10 gateways; stations load signed firmware and device identity certificates from the manufacturing PKI
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $6.8 million of monitoring-segment shipments per business day; a two-week finished-goods buffer covers normal orders; device history records must be complete before release (21 CFR 820); MES configuration changes rarely, so a daily backup is enough
manual_workaround: Ship from finished-goods stock; hold lots until MES records can be completed; no paper build path for firmware programming
dependent_systems: SYS-06 (FL-1 MES and stations); SYS-04 (released images and manufacturing PKI); SYS-07
quantified_impact_basis: Idle labor and expediting while the finished-goods buffer covers orders; deferred revenue begins after about 10 business days
single_points_of_failure: Manufacturing PKI issuing CA (HA pair at DC-1; no issuance if both fail)

description: Build, test, program, and release IV-300 pumps and wireless modules
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $4.8 million of infusion shipments per business day; a 10-day finished-goods buffer; MN-1 MES runs on an unsupported OS with no tested restore (POAM-009)
manual_workaround: Ship from finished goods; hold lots; no manual programming path
dependent_systems: SYS-06 (MN-1 MES and stations); SYS-04 (IV-300 images; legacy signing workstation); SYS-07
dependent_third_parties: Wireless module supplier (single source); component suppliers
quantified_impact_basis: Idle labor and expediting while the buffer covers orders
acquired_business_dependency: Whole process is in the acquired business: flat OT network, legacy directory, checksum-only station verification (POAM-006, POAM-007, POAM-019)
single_points_of_failure: MN-1 MES server (single instance, unsupported OS); single-source wireless module

business_process: ECG patch and home blood pressure monitor production (Plant TX-1)
description: Build, test, and release CR-100 patches (consumables) and HB-40 monitors
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: RCM depends on a steady supply of CR-100 patches; about 10 days of patch inventory at the distribution center and at customers; HB-40 retail stock covers about 6 weeks
manual_workaround: Ship from inventory; prioritize patches for RCM customers
dependent_systems: SYS-06 (TX-1 MES and stations); SYS-04; SYS-07
dependent_third_parties: ECG sensor supplier (single source); contract manufacturer CMO-2 (HB-40 subassembly)
quantified_impact_basis: Idle labor; patch allocation limits RCM new enrollments after about 7 days

business_process: Order fulfillment, distribution, and UDI traceability
description: Orders, shipping from the TX-1 distribution center, serial and UDI records that trace each unit to its customer
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About $19.2 million of revenue per business day; hospitals depend on consumables and replacement pumps; serial and UDI traceability is needed to find every affected unit in a correction or removal (21 CFR 806); ERP is SOX-relevant
manual_workaround: Manual shipping log on paper for urgent consumables and replacements; back-entry into the ERP on recovery
dependent_third_parties: ERP SaaS vendor; freight carriers; warehouse automation vendor
quantified_impact_basis: About 62% of daily shipments are same-week orders that would be deferred (about $12 million a business day); expediting costs added

description: Hospital calls and tickets; troubleshooting; on-site repairs and installations; USB updates for legacy devices
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Hospitals expect same-day response for devices in clinical use; support calls are often the first sign of a complaint or a security event
manual_workaround: Phone line forwarded to regional service managers; paper call log copied into ticketing and the eQMS on recovery
dependent_third_parties: Ticketing SaaS vendor (subcontractor BA); telephony carrier
acquired_business_dependency: IV-300 service tools from the acquired business are not yet in the enterprise ticketing system

business_process: Consumer companion app and HB-40 consumer support
description: App account, reading sync, reports the user shares with a doctor, and consumer support
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: HB-40 stores 200 readings and syncs later, so an outage does not lose readings; app store reviews and consumer trust drive reputation; a data loss would trigger FTC rule analysis
manual_workaround: Readings stay on the device; users can view readings on the monitor display
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider B; mobile operating system platforms and app stores; consumer support vendor
quantified_impact_basis: Support volume and app store refunds

business_process: Ultrasound image archive and US-20 app services (DDC)
description: US-20 images uploaded from the tablet app to the DDC archive for hospital users; worklist and sharing
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: US-20 scanning works offline; images queue on the tablet; hospitals rely on the archive for review and documentation
manual_workaround: Tablets hold queued images; clinicians document from the tablet
quantified_impact_basis: SL-1 service credits for the image archive feature

description: Design history files; risk management files; 510(k) preparation including section 524B content and the AI-001 submission
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Submission dates are planned months ahead; records must be complete for FDA inspection
manual_workaround: Work from exported controlled documents; defer approvals

description: Close, consolidation, 10-Q and 10-K preparation, and 8-K filings
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: The MTD drops to 48 hours in the quarter-end and filing windows because of SEC deadlines; an 8-K Item 1.05 must be filed within 4 business days of a materiality determination even during an outage
manual_workaround: Filing agent can prepare and submit filings from counsel's systems; close uses exported trial balances
quantified_impact_basis: Staff overtime; the impact is regulatory and reputational

description: Payroll for 12,000 employees; plant timekeeping; onboarding and terminations
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll runs biweekly and plant staff are hourly; missing payroll has legal and retention impact; same-day access removal at termination depends on HR events
manual_workaround: Repeat prior payroll through the payroll provider; plant time captured on paper; HR calls the service desk to disable accounts
acquired_business_dependency: MN-1 timekeeping runs on a legacy system until 2027-03

business_process: Supplier management, procurement, and contract manufacturing
description: Purchase orders, supplier quality, contract manufacturer releases, and supplier security reviews
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Component lead times are weeks; a short outage delays orders but not production
manual_workaround: Phone and email orders to top suppliers from printed lists
single_points_of_failure: Single-source wireless module (MN-1) and ECG sensor (TX-1)
